old: we sailed until we came to Aeaea, the island where dawn
new: we sailed until we came to the Aeaean island, where dawn
reason: Butler writes "the Aeaean island"; the form "Aeaea" occurs nowhere in PG #1727 or in any accepted Book (which print only "Aeaean", e.g. B10 "came to the Aeaean island"), so the draft introduces a name form Butler never uses, contrary to its own note that already-Greek names are kept exactly as Butler spells them.

old: Halfway up it there is a large cave
new: In the middle of it there is a large cave
reason: Butler: "In the middle of it there is a large cavern"; "halfway up" supplies a vertical position Butler does not state.

old: Three times a day she spits her waters out
new: Three times a day she vomits her waters up
reason: Butler: "Three times in the day does she vomit forth her waters"; "spits" softens the image, and the same verb is kept as "vomited it up" at P19, so one Butler word now has two renderings in this Book.

old: began to show in heaven, whereon she returned inland
new: began to show in heaven. At that she returned inland
reason: Butler's connective "whereon" is left standing as a dead archaism; GLOSSARY (rows added at Book 4) renders it "at that", and no accepted Book 9-11 keeps it, while this same draft renders the other Book 12 instance (P30) in modern English.

old: the great and clever goddess Circe
new: the great and cunning goddess Circe
reason: Butler: "the great and cunning goddess Circe", the same stock epithet accepted as "great and cunning goddess" at B10-P11 and B11-P0 (the latter in the identical fair-wind formula); "clever" breaks the recurring formula and weakens it.

old: even so did Scylla lift these struggling men up to her rock and devour them at the mouth of her den
new: even so did Scylla land these panting creatures on her rock and munch them up at the mouth of her den
reason: Butler: "even so did Scylla land these panting creatures on her rock and munch them up"; the draft drops the simile's closing half ("land" as a fisherman lands fish, "panting" answering "gasping"), and the drafter's note claims "munch them up" is present when the candidate prints "devour".

old: The men were dismayed at this
new: The men were in despair at this
reason: Butler: "The men were in despair at this"; "dismayed" softens it and puts the edition's reserved "dismay" word (GLOSSARY: dismay vs. grief kept apart) where Butler has despair.
Butler: "Ulysses,' said he, 'you are cruel"; "hard" softens Eurylochus's accusation in what Butler calls an insolent answer (ODY-RULES: no softening of anger).

old: the gods soon began to show signs
new: the gods at once began to show signs
reason: Butler: "the gods began at once to show signs and wonders"; "soon" loses the immediacy.
Butler: "raised our masts"; the plural is Butler's and concrete detail is kept exactly (GLOSSARY Voice and form).

old: The mast struck the helmsman on the head as it fell, crushing
new: The mast fell on the head of the helmsman in the ship’s stern, crushing
reason: Butler: "The mast fell upon the head of the helmsman in the ship's stern"; the draft drops where the helmsman stood.

PUNCTUATION §4 (D15) takes the modern standard form and accepted Books 3 and 5 print "seagulls"/"seagull"; scripts/compound_drift.py fails on this key ("closed in book03; hyphenated in ody"), contrary to the drafter's note that no rule applies.

old: from her keel, which drifted off by itself, and tore
new: from her keel (which drifted about by itself) and tore
reason: Butler: "from her keel (which drifted about by itself)"; ODY-RULES / PUNCTUATION §6 bind that Butler's parenthetical asides keep their parentheses, and "drifted off" changes "drifted about" (aimlessly) to "away".

old: a backstay of stout ox-hide still
new: a backstay of stout ox hide still
reason: Accepted B02 ("ropes of twisted ox hide") and B10 ("a prime ox hide") print the noun open; the hyphenated noun here is a cross-Book compound drift (D15).
Accepted Book 5 prints "seawater"; scripts/compound_drift.py fails on this key ("closed in book05; open in ody") under D15.
